skill.name: hook-development
skill.description: Guides developers through building Claude Code hooks that validate tool use, enforce workflow rules, load context, and test hook configurations.
skill.summary: Create and test Claude Code hooks for safer automated workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, defensive validators, or expected shell helper scripts. The review confirms real risks in the hook test helper and in advanced logging examples that can expose raw hook payloads.

remediation.suggestion: Avoid bash -c with concatenated paths. Invoke the hook through arrays, quote arguments, and reject paths containing shell metacharacters.

remediation.issue: Database logging example stores raw hook input.
remediation.suggestion: Use parameterized queries, redact secrets, and require explicit opt-in before sending hook payloads to external systems.

remediation.issue: Audit logging example writes raw payloads to a hidden home file.
remediation.suggestion: Redact sensitive fields, set restrictive permissions, document retention, and prefer project-local opt-in logging.

remediation.issue: Examples use predictable temporary file names.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp, trap cleanup, and restrictive permissions for state, cache, and test files.

content.value_statement: Claude Code hooks are powerful but easy to configure incorrectly. This skill gives patterns, scripts, and checks for safer hook design.
actual_capabilities: Explains command and prompt-based hook event types.
Shows plugin and settings hook configuration formats.
Provides example validators for Bash and file write events.
Includes scripts to lint, test, and validate hook configurations.
Documents migration paths from command hooks to prompt hooks.
limitations: Does not install hooks or modify user projects by itself.
Examples require local review before production use.
Shell helpers assume bash, jq, and compatible Unix tooling.
Prompt-based decisions depend on model behavior and policy wording.

use_cases.title: Add Tool Validation
use_cases.description: Create PreToolUse checks that approve safe commands and block risky file or shell operations.

use_cases.title: Package Plugin Hooks
use_cases.description: Build portable hook configurations that use plugin-relative paths and clear event matchers.

use_cases.title: Review Hook Safety
use_cases.description: Audit hook scripts for quoting, timeouts, input validation, and sensitive data handling.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Hook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code PreToolUse hook for Write operations that checks paths and explains each decision.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Command Hook
prompt_templates.scenario: Move from shell logic to a prompt hook.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert my existing Bash validation hook into a prompt-based hook with equivalent approval and denial criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Hook Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design test cases for this hook, including allowed actions, denied actions, malformed input, and timeout behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Advanced Hook Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this hook configuration for security, portability, sensitive data exposure, race conditions, and maintainability risks.

output_examples.input: Review a proposed PreToolUse hook that blocks risky Bash commands.
output: Identifies the correct hook event and matcher.
Separates simple allow rules from denial criteria.
Recommends tests for safe, dangerous, and ambiguous commands.

output_examples.input: Migrate a shell-based file validation hook to a prompt hook.
output: Summarizes the original checks in plain language.
Creates prompt criteria for system paths, credentials, traversal, and content risk.
Notes where deterministic checks may still be useful.

output_examples.input: Audit hook utility scripts before publishing a plugin.
output: Flags unsafe shell construction and raw payload logging.
Suggests safer argument handling and redaction.
Lists verification steps for linting and sample execution.

best_practices: Prefer prompt hooks for complex intent checks and command hooks for fast deterministic checks.
Validate and quote all command hook inputs before using them.
Test hooks with representative allowed, denied, and malformed inputs.
anti_patterns: Logging full hook payloads to local files or external systems.
Passing untrusted script paths into shell command strings.
Relying on hook execution order for shared state.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps create Claude Code hooks for validation, context loading, workflow enforcement, and plugin automation.

faq.question: Does it favor prompt hooks or command hooks?
faq.answer: It recommends prompt hooks for complex decisions and command hooks for fast deterministic checks.

faq.question: Can it validate hook configuration files?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance and a helper script for checking hook structure and common configuration issues.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex can use the guidance to author or review Claude Code hook files in a repository.

faq.question: Are the shell examples production ready?
faq.answer: They are starting points. Review paths, quoting, logging, and environment handling before production use.

faq.question: What is the main safety concern?
faq.answer: Hooks process tool input, so unsafe shell construction or raw logging can expose data or run unintended commands.
